summary: Flathead/Lincoln County platform lookout built in 1929 with a log cabin; a forest fire burned it; the trail now leads to its historic site. The forest is disputed.

facts.status_note: Burned in a forest fire; Visit Montana calls the trail's destination the historic site of Locke Lookout

access.note: Krinklehorn-Locke Mountain Trail (96) is a 2.0-mile National Forest trail that leads to the historic site of Locke Lookout

visit.trail_note: Trail 96 begins at Trail 358 and connects the Krinklehorn Trail with the Whitefish Divide Trail

events.note: 20-foot platform tower with a log cabin

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts places the lookout in the Flathead National Forest; the Visit Montana trail listing names the Kootenai National Forest map. We could not settle which forest. Record kept as Flathead.

notes_for_editor: Only two sources, both short. The 1929 build date comes from Forest Lookouts alone; no burn date is given anywhere we read. The forest is disputed (Flathead vs Kootenai map). The FFLA list also has a separate 'Locke Ridge' tower record (Gone, 48.80984 -114.73258); it may be a different structure or a duplicate, so check before merging. Search results about Apgar and Loneman were other lookouts and are not used.
